cards.title: Everything that happened, in order
cards.text: 6 on-track passes, 1 pit stop, 1 car not classified.

cards.title: 8 places changed hands on track before the first lap was done
cards.text: 22 cars into the first corner on cold tyres and full tanks.
bullets: Bearman gained the most by the end of it, 2 places
cards.note: Most of this is the pack sorting itself out. Some of it decides the sprint.

cards.title: 1 incident looked at
cards.text: Logged by race control during the sprint.
bullets: Lap 1: Sainz and Bottas, starting procedure infringement

cards.title: Alonso starts from the pit lane. Where does he finish?
cards.text: 24 laps to make up ground from there.
cards.reveal: Out of the points. The exact place comes at the flag.

cards.title: Who has the fastest lap on the board at the flag?
cards.text: It usually lands late, when the car is light and the track has rubber all over it.
cards.reveal: Norris on lap 5, 1:14.881, in a McLaren.

cards.title: Norris: 1:14.881
cards.text: The quickest anybody went all sprint, in a McLaren.
bullets: Set on lap 5 of 24, early for a fastest lap, with plenty of fuel still on board
A sprint has never paid a point for it

cards.title: Track between 24°C and 30°C during the sprint
cards.text: Track temperature changes how much grip the tyres find and how fast they wear. No rain was recorded during the sprint.

cards.title: Hamilton hit 320 km/h
cards.text: The trap reads one fixed point on the lap, so a car can go faster elsewhere. And the fastest car in a straight line is often not the fastest car over a lap.
bullets: Hamilton did it in a Ferrari
cards.note: Top speed says as much about wing level, and about sitting in somebody's tow, as it does about the engine.

cards.title: Leclerc had the quickest median racing lap
cards.text: No lap 1, no laps in or out of the pits, nothing behind the safety car or the VSC, and the slow outliers trimmed. It does not always match the result.

cards.title: Stroll: 8 laps within a second of the car ahead
cards.text: The longest unbroken run like it in the sprint, from lap 10 to lap 17, at racing speed.
bullets: 5 other drivers had a run of five laps or more like it
cards.note: Following closely costs the car downforce and cooks the front tyres, so sitting there is harder than it looks.

cards.title: 1 lap time deleted
cards.text: The white line is the track, and the lap simply stops counting if you leave it.
bullets: Keep doing it and it turns into a penalty

cards.title: Alonso: from the pit lane, P18 at the flag
How far behind was Leclerc at the flag?
cards.text: 24 laps, about 30 minutes of racing. Put a number on the gap to the winner.

cards.title: 21 of 22 cars never stopped
cards.text: One set of tyres took most of the field to the flag.
bullets: On one set the whole way: Mediums for 19, softs for Leclerc and Bearman
cards.note: Every lap you stretch is a lap you do not lose in the pit lane.

cards.title: Russell wins it
cards.text: P1 Russell · P2 Leclerc · P3 Norris.
bullets: After 24 laps, Leclerc crossed the line 1.360s behind
cards.note: Less than the time it takes to read this sentence.
